overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that gpt-5.5 with function tools and no explicit reasoning_effort would route to Chat Completions, but the code at main.py:1127-1131 still contains the old conditional logic that routes gpt-5.4+ with explicit reasoning_effort to Responses, and the new gpt-5.4/5.5 default-to-none logic only applies when reasoning_effort is unset or 'none'. When a user explicitly sets reasoning_effort: low on gpt-5.5, the old bridge condition still fires and routes to Responses, triggering the 400 error.
why_it_breaks: The PR's new comment at line 1128 says gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5 default to "none" and serve tools on Chat Completions, but this only applies when reasoning_effort is unset or explicitly 'none'. The original code comment (removed in the edit) stated that unset reasoning_effort means medium server-side and Chat Completions rejects function tools whenever reasoning is on. When the user explicitly sets reasoning_effort: low on gpt-5.5, the bridge logic still treats it as an explicit effort and routes to the Responses API, where the provider returns HTTP 400 for function tools with reasoning_effort on gpt-5.5. The agent overlooked that the 'default to none' behavior is conditional on the absence of an explicit reasoning_effort value, not a model-wide property.
